title: SaaS microservices auth and data plane
blurb: User auth service, product API, analytics pipeline, and shared identity. STRIDE-friendly system interview.

project.name: Cloud-native SaaS platform
project.description: Multi-tenant SaaS with OAuth login, product API, and analytics export.

dataflows.name: Product API validates token with auth

threats.name: Cross-tenant data access
threats.description: Broken object-level auth lets tenant A read tenant B records.

threats.name: Token theft and replay
threats.description: Stolen bearer token used from another client to call product APIs.

threats.name: Over-broad analytics export
threats.description: Exporter copies PII or secrets into a lower-trust analytics store.

threats.name: Lateral movement between services
threats.description: Compromised product API calls auth or other services with overly broad mesh identity.

mitigations.name: Tenant-bound authorization
mitigations.description: Enforce tenant id from the token on every object access; deny cross-tenant identifiers.

mitigations.name: Short-lived tokens and binding
mitigations.description: Short access TTL, refresh rotation, audience restriction; consider DPoP/mTLS for high-risk clients.

mitigations.name: Minimized export schemas
mitigations.description: Allowlisted fields, tokenization of PII, separate analytics keys, and access reviews.

mitigations.name: mTLS and least-privilege service identity
mitigations.description: Service mesh mTLS, explicit allow policies per RPC, no cluster-wide credentials.

prompts.title: Run a quick STRIDE pass on the Product API. Name one threat per letter that fits this model.
prompts.answerMarkdown: Spoofing: stolen bearer token at the edge. Tampering: request body that changes another tenant's object id. Repudiation: missing audit on admin exports. Information disclosure: verbose errors or analytics over-export. DoS: unauthenticated expensive search on the gateway. Elevation: product service identity that can call auth admin APIs. Tie each to a component or flow in the model.

prompts.title: How do you prove multi-tenant isolation is real, not just a middleware claim?
prompts.answerMarkdown: Show object-level checks tied to tenant claim, negative tests for cross-tenant ids, storage keys partitioned by tenant where required, and support/admin impersonation controls. Mention logs that do not leak cross-tenant identifiers casually. Verification: automated BOLA tests in CI plus production canaries.

prompts.title: The analytics export is new. What do you challenge in a design review?
prompts.answerMarkdown: What fields leave the data plane, who can query the sink, retention, legal basis, and whether secrets/tokens can appear. Demand a schema allowlist, encryption, and an owner. Ask how a tenant deletion or export request propagates. Residual risk: analytics VPC is still a high-value store.
